takeaways: DOJ antitrust probe covers beef pricing at 8 retailers: Kroger, Publix, Walmart, Albertsons, Aldi, Ahold Delhaize USA, Costco, Amazon.
The DOJ letters (dated July 16) ask for retail and wholesale beef prices, costs, margins and pricing strategy, so expect retailers to scrutinize their suppliers' costs.
Walmart: the White House said on July 6 that Walmart would cut ground beef about 15%. The claim came from the President, and I found no Walmart statement confirming it.
Cocoa has fallen from its highs and 2026 is on track for a second year of surplus, but retail chocolate has been slow to follow.

Cocoa prices have fallen from record highs and 2026 is on track for a second year of surplus. Analysts expected retail relief by Halloween, but chocolate stayed high through Easter because supply chains were tight. Check shelf prices before promising anything.
Retail beef set record highs in 2026 and the cattle herd is near historic lows. A Fortune headline from April says prices won't come down until about 2028. Treat that as an opinion, not a forecast.

talkingPoints: Your retail customers are under DOJ scrutiny on beef margins, so ask distributors how they plan to document cost and price changes.
Ground beef is the political price item right now. Ask what end users are doing on case-ready ground price points.
Ask whether customers expect cocoa relief to show up in chocolate pricing before the holidays.
